scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on sshswitch, the multilayer switch serving Campus 2. Its
VLAN 5 SVI bridge interface, br_v5 (IP 10.5.0.254/24), has been
administratively brought down — its state is <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with
no UP or LOWER_UP flags. This interface is the Layer 3 gateway for all
VLAN 5 hosts (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, dc_pc5 at 10.5.0.5).

Because br_v5 is down, ARP requests for the gateway IP 10.5.0.254 go
unanswered, so VLAN 5 hosts cannot resolve the gateway MAC and have no
path off their subnet. Layer 2 switching within VLAN 5 still works
normally through switch4's hardware bridge, which is why intra-VLAN
pings (PC1↔PC2) succeed without needing the gateway. The effect is
exclusively limited to inter-subnet (routed) traffic. VLAN 6 is
unaffected because its equivalent bridge, br_v6, remains UP with IP
10.6.0.254/24 responding normally, as confirmed by PC3 successfully
pinging its gateway.

The two member interfaces of br_v5 — bond0.5 (the LACP trunk sub-
interface toward router17) and eth0.5 (the VLAN-tagged sub-interface
toward switch4) — are both UP. The bridge itself is the only broken
element. The startup script correctly calls `ip link set br_v5 up`, so
this interface was shut down post-boot by the injected fault.

Root cause: br_v5 on sshswitch was administratively shut down after
startup, destroying the VLAN 5 SVI and blocking all routed traffic for
that VLAN.

Corrective fix: Run `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch. This restores
the VLAN 5 SVI immediately; no routing reconfiguration is required as
all other config (IP address, OSPF advertisement, bridge membership) is
intact.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names sshswitch as the device with the faulty br_v5 SVI.
The report explicitly names the VLAN 5 SVI bridge interface br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24) as the failed component.
The writeup explicitly identifies VLAN 5 as impacted by br_v5 being down and states VLAN 6 is unaffected with br_v6 up and responding.
The agent explicitly recommends running 'ip link set br_v5 up' on sshswitch, which matches the expected fix and will restore the VLAN 5 SVI.

The log clearly shows br_v5 is DOWN and that hosts in VLAN 5 cannot reach 10.5.0.254 while VLAN6 and intra-VLAN traffic work, so the core conclusion is well supported. A couple of claims (that the startup script explicitly sets br_v5 up and that all member subinterfaces’ UP state is shown) are not fully evidenced in the log.
